title: Adaptive affinity-based concurrency limiter and graceful timeout strategy for reranking endpoint
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint shows long-tail p95/p99 latency spikes under mixed workloads (short queries, long-candidate lists, and enterprise bulk calls). Existing hard token caps and uniform microbatching are either conservative (wasteful throughput) or brittle (tail latency regressions).

Goal: Implement an adaptive concurrency limiter that uses affinity signals (model shard, cached KV presence, customer SLA tier) to prefer scheduling low-cost candidates and to shape per-request timeouts. Complement this with a graceful timeout/fallback path that returns partial but high-confidence rerank outputs when deadlines are hit. The feature should preserve or improve NDCG@10 and keep p95 latency within SLA bounds while improving throughput and cost for standard workloads.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for the rerank endpoint decreases by >=10% on aggregate test workload or stays within +/-5% of baseline while throughput increases by >=7%
NDCG@10 regression against baseline < 0.3 points on production-sampled prompts (A/B evaluation)
Can be toggled via runtime feature flag and rolled back automatically if p95 increases by >10% or NDCG@10 drops >0.5
Support per-customer QoS tiers where premium customers can opt into lower latency at higher cost (documented API options)
Comprehensive unit, integration, and load tests are present and passing in CI with synthetic long-tail workloads
technical_notes: Affinity signals: prefer candidates with hot KV cache hits, same model shard to avoid cross-device overhead, and cached embeddings. Maintain an affinity score per candidate computed at filter time.

Concurrency limiter: token-bucket style but weighted by affinity. Low-affinity candidates consume more concurrency credit; high-affinity consume less. Allow dynamic scaling of bucket refill rate by observed p95 latency percentile.

Microbatching: introduce latency-targeted microbatch sizes. For small requests (<200 tokens total) prioritize tight latency (microbatch size 1-4). For larger candidate sets, form microbatches that respect per-candidate affinity windows to reduce KV thrashing.

Token-length admission: pre-tokenize candidate text at filter stage to compute exact token budgets; reject/trim candidates server-side when per-request token budget would exceed configured hard limit.

Graceful timeout path: when a soft deadline is reached, return partial scores with confidence metadata. Confidence computed from prefix length, model logit margin heuristics, and candidate affinity. Optionally rerun top-K local rescoring using a cheap scoring model for fallback quality improvement.
Preemption: long in-flight low-affinity microbatches are preemptible; preemption yields partial scores for those candidates and frees slots for high-affinity requests.

Observability: add counters for affinity distribution, preemption events, fallback returns, partial-response rate, and per-tier latency/throughput. Surface p50/p95/p99 by affinity bucket and customer tier.
Safety: ensure deterministic ordering of candidates in partial responses and tag responses as partial to prevent downstream consumer misinterpretation. Add idempotency markers for retries.

Compatibility: keep existing API unchanged; expose optional query params: qos_tier (string) and allow_partial (bool). Default remains previous behavior (allow_partial=false) until rollout enables it for all traffic.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and API opts (allow_partial, qos_tier)
Unit + integration tests merged behind flag
Canary 1: enable for internal traffic and internal test customers (5% of prod traffic) with read-only monitoring for 48h
Canary 2: enable allow_partial for non-critical customers (25%) with automated rollback if p95 > baseline * 1.10 or NDCG@10 delta < -0.5
Full rollout: 100% after 7 days of stable canary and manual review of A/B metrics
Enterprise opt-in: offer qos_tier premium immediately after full rollout
Post-rollout: monitor for 30 days; schedule a follow-up runbook and postmortem if rollback triggered
test_plan: Unit tests for affinity scoring, token admission, and concurrency accounting
Integration tests simulating mixed short/long workloads and verifying preemption and fallback instrumentation
E2E load test in staging with production-like traffic replay (72h) measuring p50/p95/p99, throughput, and partial-return rate
A/B experiment comparing baseline vs new strategy on production-sampled prompts for 2 weeks measuring NDCG@10 and business metrics
Chaos test: inject KV cache miss storms and slow model shard responses to validate graceful behavior and automated rollback
